topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, setting expectations about the complexity and clinical relevance of the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals, Nomenclature, and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the overarching architecture and biological roles of complement, clarify historical naming conventions, and explain the central biochemical function of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the initiation and progression of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that converge on surface C3 convertase deposition.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Activated Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the primary functional outcomes of complement activation: opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the cellular and soluble regulatory mechanisms that restrict complement activity to protect host tissues from accidental destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Presentations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical consequences and disease phenotypes associated with deficiencies across different complement pathway components.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Pathogen Evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how pathogens evolve specific countermeasures to subvert complement recognition and clearance, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
